Project 01

Solar Panel Model

2024 Algoma Science Fair · Grade 10 · Team project

A dual-axis solar tracker that automatically repositions itself throughout the day to follow the sun and maximize energy capture — built around an Arduino control system and photoresistor light sensors, in my first hands-on project with either.

Recurring wiring failures and a frame that tipped under its own weight became the real engineering challenge, pushing me toward a more resourceful, test-and-iterate build process — a mindset I've carried into every project since.

🏆 1st Place, Intermediate Division + Computer Science & Computer Engineering Awards

Project 02

VEX Robotics — Founding Team

Founding Member & Lead Driver · Gr. 12

As a founding member of St. Mary's College's first VEX Robotics team, I helped design, build, and program a competition robot from scratch — with no existing program, parts inventory, or senior members to learn from.

Selected as lead driver for my hands-on familiarity with the robot, I combined that build knowledge with in-match strategy to help our first-year team take the City Championship.

🏆 City Champions, VEX Robotics Tournament (founding year)

Project 03

Ultrasonic Walking Stick

Individual project · Gr. 12

An assistive cane that uses ultrasonic sensing to detect obstacles in a visually impaired user's path and alert them before contact — designed and built independently for the Senior category of the regional STEM fair.

Field testing confirmed the device delivered reliable, near-instantaneous feedback at normal walking speed across a range of obstacle types and placements.

🏆 3rd Place, Senior Category
